Is that making the 2028 target more difficult to get to, or is it just because the quarter is so strong in Investment Banking and you are taking advantage of that? What's going on there [to get to] at least to circa 50% [RWAs]? And then secondly, actually the equity trading. 45% growth would be seen in any normal period as a very, very strong performance. But when the US peers are doing about 70% growth, by definition therefore you have lost share versus them. So how has that been looked at internally? Is it seen as a blowout, very strong quarter or are you seeing it as losing share essentially?",
  "answer_quote": "Okay, so on the RWAs, we lent in a little bit in the quarter in RWAs in the Investment Bank. It's up about 1% quarter on quarter, about 40% of the growth year on year was FX, so you can ignore that. I'll come back to this a bit more fully when I talk about Equities, but our objective here is to maintain the discipline around [RWAs], and if we do deploy a little bit more, then we're looking for revenue. So you can see revenue over RWAs has gone up to 7.7%, that's a hundred basis points up year on year. So this capital efficiency is really what we are driving. The second, so let put a different perspective to this, clearly we continue to grow the rest of the bank. Notably in that percentage is the deployment of the advanced model in US cards, which is going to meaningfully change that percentage. That was always in our plan, so that's the piece that you're sort of missing. On Equities, for us, market share is an output. So scale matters in this business. We are very, very well aware of that, but at the same time we have scale and we're showing that, because as I said before to a previous question, we would not have had the Equities capability to get a result like the one that we had. So we see it as a good reflection of the investment that we've put in place in previous years and it is years, it's back to 2022. And for us, our objective is returns in this business. So it is about revenue over RWAs and it's also, I mean we talk about discipline, what does that actually mean? It means returns on the capital that we deploy. So is revenue over RWAs going up? Yes it is, but also are those returns flowing through to the bottom line? So expect us to be taking risk actions that are commensurate with the environment that we see around us, which we do see as uncertain and we do see as volatile. So if you look at our trading revenues and it is page 40, you can see that that bell curve of daily trading has shifted to the right and that there was one loss day in [H126] and zero in the quarter. That is what we want. We don't want enormous days and loss days. So that risk management's really important. You can see that bar is largely stable. By the way, we're taking the same approach on our Banking side. So if you look at our corporate lending line, it's relatively low. That tells you we're doing a lot of hedging, and one of the reasons that our DCM performance was below that of our peers is on Leveraged Finance. We walked away from some opportunities because of the return and the risk involved. So we've taken quite a defensive posture, but we think that's the right thing given the environment and we are getting the returns that we expect from the business.",
